title: Software platform: ROS Indigo / Ubuntu Trusty, armhf userland, Rockchip-class SoC
evidence: All 106 debs: control Architecture=armhf; 104 debs Version 2.3.1c1-4573-g1406f3b-trusty, ros-indigo-filters 1.1.1, ros-indigo-robotviz 2.6.1c1v4-4-g8006fd8-trusty. ELF scan of data.tar: 283 ELF files = 278 ARM32 (266 stripped + 12 unstripped) + 3 RISC-V32 (micro-laser firmware) + 2 x86-64; robot-settings postinst branches on `uname -p` (aarch64/x86_64); robot-settings firmware/rosconsole/aarch64/indigo/librosconsole.so is ELF ARM 32-bit; robot-settings usr/bin/user_monitor.sh references /sys/kernel/config/usb_gadget/rockchip/UDC and adbd.sh.
status: CONFIRMED (armhf/trusty/indigo); STRONGLY_SUPPORTED (aarch64 kernel with 32-bit userland on a Rockchip SoC)
impact: Defines the toolchain/ABI any custom node or replacement binary must match (32-bit ARM, glibc of Ubuntu 14.04, Boost 1.54, OpenCV 2.4, PCL 1.7/1.8).
remediation: Build any added ROS nodes with the same cross toolchain (ros indigo, trusty armhf); do not assume a 64-bit userland.
description: The whole stack is ROS Indigo (Python 2.7) built for Ubuntu 14.04 (trusty) armhf. Directory name firmware/rosconsole/aarch64 holds a 32-bit ARM library, and postinst checks for aarch64, which together indicate a 64-bit kernel running a 32-bit userland. user_monitor.sh refers to the Rockchip USB gadget configfs. This is a static inference; no live system was examined.

title: Package is multi-model; C40 launch profile identified (keenon_robot_C40.launch)

C40, C40H, C55, C30, T*, G*, M*, W*, S100.
status: CONFIRMED (launch defaults); UNKNOWN (which launch file is active on a given unit)
impact: The package contains configuration for ~30 Keenon models; the active model on a unit is chosen by /home/peanut/launch_config/keenon_robot.launch which is preserved across updates (preinst/config_setting.py), not by this package alone.

title: Mapping, localization and navigation architecture
component: cartographer, peanut-localization, location-fusion, keenon-vslam, move-base, kplanner, teb-*
evidence: cartographer include/cartographer_1.launch: cartographer_node -configuration_basename keenon_common.lua (2D, use_odometry=true, use_landmarks=true, tracking_frame=laser_link), cartographer_occupancy_grid_node -resolution 0.05, auto_denoise_node, label_filter_node; gmapping.launch (slam_gmapping). peanut_localization_node (150 param names, libpcl 1.8.1.99, libcreate_local_map.a). location_fusion_node (libmyorocos-bfl). move_base_teb.launch: base_global_planner=kplanner/KPlannerROS, base_local_planner=teb_local_planner/TebLocalPlannerROS; C40 move_base_params.yaml recovery_behaviors clear_static_recovery + rotation_escape_recovery. C40 teb params: max_vel_x 0.8, max_vel_theta 0.6/1.0, acc_lim_x 0.7/0.3. C40 costmap footprint is an 11-point polygon about 0.62 m long x 0.54 m wide.
impact: Mapping uses Cartographer 2D pbstream maps; run-time localization is a PCL-registration node fused (EKF/BFL) with labels and mono VSLAM; navigation is classic move_base with a custom global planner and TEB.
remediation: None (descriptive).
description: Two SLAM back-ends are launched (cartographer for map building, gmapping available), localization is separate (peanut_localization) and fused by location_fusion. Costmap observation sources for C40 include /scan, /fdl/obs_cliff, /fdl/obs_low, /sy_tof_dev_node/depth/points, /bump, /edge_laser_front_cloud, /low_cloud_left, /low_cloud_right, /mx/cloud1, carpet clouds (costmap_common_params.yaml).

title: Cleaning actuators controlled through the chassis node (brushes, water pump, suction fan, dust box)
evidence: chassis ELF strings (STATIC_REFERENCE): /water_pump, /water_suction_motor, /motor_air, /motor_edge, /motor_edge_cover, /motor_roll, /motor_sweep, /motor_wash_brush_rod, /motor_wash_brush_switch, /motor_roll_brush_rod_stm32, /rake_rod, /disc_brush, /roll_brush, /dis_rod, /BC_DustBox, /clean_devices_control, /clean_device_switch_status, /debug_chassis/start_water_value_and_water_time, /chassis/suction_switch, /self_clean_task, /carpet_detection_switch, /urgency_stop, /light_switch, /steering_engine_switch. C40 chassis_params.yaml: port /dev/ttyUSBStm32, wheel_gauge 377.4 mm, wheel_perimeter 439.2 mm, water_suction (fan gear) 80, WaterControlLow pulse control (water_pump_low 30), stage*_edge_brush_value, stage*_wash_brush_value/rod, stage*_roll_brush_value. keenon_clean_msgs: clean_device_control(device_type, device_lock), self_clean_status, carpetStatus, task_manager_report stage TASK_stage_residual_water. robot_monitor_params.yaml: dust_box error 140601, motor error bits 1404xx.
impact: Confirms a wet-scrubber style cleaning head: roll/wash brushes with lift rods, edge brush, vacuum/suction fan, water pump with pulse control and a dust box, all driven from an STM32 over serial.
remediation: Live-test actuator topics only on a safe test unit; do not publish to them on a unit in service.
description: No actuator is driven directly by a ROS node on the main CPU; the chassis node translates topics to an STM32 serial protocol (/dev/ttyUSBStm32). The protocol itself (libslam_comm_lib / chassis) was not reverse engineered.

title: STM32 / peripheral MCU link and firmware update (IAP) path
evidence: robot-settings usr/bin/usb_scan strings: symlink targets /dev/ttyUSBStm32, /dev/ttyUSBLoRa, /dev/ttyUSBLidar, /dev/ttyUSBLabel, /dev/ttyUSBSchedule, /dev/ttyUSBDoorCtl, /dev/aruco_location*, netlink monitor, GPIO power via /sys/class/gpio and /etc/power_*. ros_update (libcpprest usr/bin/ros_update) strings: "mode: peripheral board", "mode:direct download", "mode:indirect download", "Enter encoder IAP mode!", "wait bootloader signal...", "SOH:%03d" (XMODEM/YMODEM-style framing), crc16_ibm, MD5 check, /dev/ttyUSBStm32; function names update_stm32_from_bin. udev rules created by auto_make_port.py: KERNELS=="..", SUBSYSTEM=="tty", MODE:="0666", GROUP:="dialout", SYMLINK+="ttyUSB...". manifest/package here ships no STM32 .bin (base_station-app belongs to another package).
status: CONFIRMED (strings); STRONGLY_SUPPORTED (STM32 IAP over serial from ros_update); framing details NOT_ANALYZED
impact: The OTA service can reflash the peripheral MCU (and encoder board) over the serial link; the MCU firmware itself is not part of this package.
remediation: Treat the update service as able to modify MCU firmware; protect it accordingly (see ROS-044).
description: Device aliases ttyUSB* are created by usb_scan (netlink monitoring of USB/serial) rather than static udev rules (50-keenon.rules is emptied/removed by postinst).

title: rosbridge WebSocket servers (ports 9090 and 9091) without authentication or TLS
evidence: robot_common.launch includes $(find rosbridge_server)/launch/rosbridge_websocket.launch and include/rosbridge_websocket_control.launch: args port=9091, address="" , ssl=false, authenticate=false, ns=control, plus rosapi_node. robotviz Home.js contains ws://192.168.64.20:9090 and ws://192.168.64.20:9091; calibration/config.json host_url 192.168.64.199:9090; robotviz index.js also contains a developer ws://172.16.8.13:9092. postinst replaces rosbridge_library protocol.py/publishers.py and tornado iostream.py with vendor copies.
status: CONFIRMED (launch args/client URLs); INFERRED (effective exposure; default port 9090 comes from upstream rosbridge_server which is not shipped)
impact: Anyone who can reach the robot LAN (or the AP that is bridged into it) can publish/subscribe/call any ROS topic or service over WebSocket, including motion and configuration services.
remediation: Bind to localhost or a management VLAN, enable authentication/SSL, firewall 9090/9091.
description: No authenticate=true or certificate is configured; address is empty which in rosbridge means all interfaces. Not tested live.

title: ros_update OTA service listens on HTTP (default port 9527) with upgrade/action and upgrade/status resources
evidence: ros_update strings: "http://0.0.0.0:", adjacent literals "upgrade/action", "upgrade/status", "192.168.64.10", "9527", "application/json"; websocketpp 0.8.2 server code (QBaseWebsocketServer); resources via cpprest http_listener (GET/POST); classes QLUpdateResource (update_ros_from_zip, update_general_from_zip, update_stm32_from_bin, install_package, restart_ros, stop_other_services, check_install), KeenonShell (sudo_exec_cmd, dpkg_info, unzip_package); build path /workdir/catkin_ws/src/keenon_ros/keenon_infrastructure/rest_kits/src/ros_update/*. upstart job ros_update.conf: start-stop-daemon, respawn unlimited, runs as root.
status: CONFIRMED (strings); port 9527 INFERRED from adjacent literal (LOW-MEDIUM); authentication behaviour UNKNOWN/NOT_ANALYZED
impact: A root-run, plain-HTTP update endpoint reachable from the robot LAN accepts update requests containing a package URL + md5 (string "No obj url md5").
remediation: Restrict to localhost/management network; require authentication and signed packages.
description: No TLS code path (only http:// 0.0.0.0:). No credential/token strings were found in the binary, which is not proof that no authentication exists.

title: WsServer websocket control channel and frp reverse tunnel (remote SSH)
evidence: WsServer (ARM32 stripped, websocketpp 0.8.2) strings: actions frpRestart, frpConfig, frpMapConfig, frpDisconnect, frpState, debug_close; builds shell commands "python /usr/bin/update_frpc.py <serverAddr> <serverPort> <remotePort> <token> <taskNo>", "python /usr/bin/update_map_frpc.py", "nginx -s reload", "md5sum %s", writes /etc/nginx/conf.d/mapping.conf and unzips certificate.zip to /etc/ros/runtime/remotemap/. frpc_release_arm: Go 1.16.2, fatedier/frp (client + dashboard assets). frpc_info.ini template: [ssh_robotSn] type=tcp local_ip=127.0.0.1 local_port=22 remote_port=<> with server_addr/server_port/token blank. update_frpc.py starts "./frpc_release_arm -c /etc/ros/runtime/frpc_info.ini" and kills it after 12 h. upstart Websocket_setup.conf: sleep 10; exec /usr/bin/WsServer (log /home/peanut/websocketlog.log). frpc_setup.conf has the frpc start commented out. WsServer listening port is not recoverable by string analysis (UNKNOWN).
impact: A remote party able to send the websocket message can make the robot open an outbound frp tunnel that exposes local sshd (port 22) on a server chosen by the message; message fields are placed into shell command lines (possible command injection if unsanitized - not tested).
remediation: Authenticate the websocket, validate/escape fields, bind to localhost, and pin server addresses.
description: The tunnel exposes SSH only if the attacker also knows or guesses the SSH credentials. The frp server address and token are supplied at runtime, so none are present in this package.

title: CoAP bridge server and download client (libcoap)
evidence: libcoap_bridge.so symbol classes (from mangled names): CoapServer, CleanResource, DiagnosisResource, ElevatorResource, ErrorResource, FdlResource, MotorResource, NavigationResource, PositionResource, RuntimeResource, VendorResource, powerResource, ServiceClient, SimpleActionClient. coap_bridge_server strings: QLDownloadClient subscribes /libcoap/download (keenon_ui_msgs/download_data: md5,url) and publishes /libcoap/download_result; downloads into /etc/ros/runtime/database/uuidzip/, /tmp/robot/, /work/robot/ ; uses libcurl + libkQLTftp ("QLTftp,downloading,curl_easy_perform"); shell composition `echo "..." | sudo -S sh -c "..."` and `chmod -R`. CoAP port not found (libcoap default 5683 only appears in pdu.h).
status: CONFIRMED (classes/strings); CoAP port UNKNOWN (default 5683 INFERRED, LOW)
impact: A CoAP (UDP, unauthenticated by default) interface exposes robot clean/navigation/motor/position/runtime resources, and a ROS-topic-triggered downloader fetches files by URL+md5 and installs them via sudo shell commands.
remediation: Restrict network exposure; use DTLS/PSK or remove; sign downloads.
description: The resource handlers and their authorization were not decompiled.

title: Robot internal network design (192.168.64.0/24, bridge br0) and Wi-Fi AP bridged into it
evidence: etc/network/interfaces: br0 bridge_ports eth0 eth1, address 192.168.64.20/24, gateway 192.168.64.10; etc/default/isc-dhcp-server INTERFACES="br0"; wifi/dhcpd.conf subnet 192.168.64.0/24 range 192.168.64.200-209, routers 192.168.64.20; etc/hostapd/hostapd.conf: interface=wlanAP, ssid=Keenon_robot_FFFFFF (last 6 hex digits rewritten from wlanAP MAC by set_ap_mode), bridge=br0, wpa=1, WPA-PSK, CCMP; net_gw.conf forces default route via 192.168.64.10 dev br0; upstart env ROS_IP=192.168.64.20; legacy rosenv ROS_MASTER_URI=http://192.168.64.20:11311; udev 70-persistent-net.rules names USB eth* as ethdbg (set_ethdbg_mode adds it to br0 and restarts dhcp).
impact: Lidars, modules, the Android UI board and the ROS master share one flat L2/L3 segment that the Wi-Fi AP and any debug Ethernet port are bridged into.
remediation: Separate the AP/debug interfaces from the control network; firewall inter-segment access.
description: Wired peers: UI 192.168.64.10 (gateway), robot 192.168.64.20, lidars .100/.101/.103/.104/.107, calibration host .199 (config.json), UWB 172.16.1.33:9000. (192.168.64.10 identified as gateway and also appears next to the OTA port string.)

title: Other hard-coded endpoints (cloud IP, devices, MX stereo module, NTP)
evidence: elevator_params.yaml (all models incl. C40): mqtt_server_ip 47.96.156.255, topics elevtopic_test / robottopic_test; usr/bin/check_connect SERVER_IP="47.96.156.255" (4G ping check, route via 10.64.64.64); MX stereo module IP 10.11.21.1 (vslam_available.sh, check_mx_stereo; module_tool wget ftp://<ip>/param/* with --ftp-user=anonymous); send_depth_node tcp://%s:%s (ZeroMQ + libsodium crypto_secretbox); time sync via ntpdate cn.pool.ntp.org; DHCP DNS 8.8.8.8, 114.114.114.114; resolv.conf nameserver 8.8.8.8 appended by robot_setup.
impact: Shows outbound dependencies: one fixed cloud IP, China NTP pool, public DNS; MX module is reached over FTP anonymous and ZMQ.
remediation: Review whether the test topic names / fixed IP should ship in production.
description: No MQTT client code was found in any ELF; the broker parameter consumer is UNKNOWN.

title: 4G modem and ppp support scripts (largely legacy)
evidence: system/conf/wvdial.conf (APN UNIM2M.NJM2MAPN, Phone *99#, Modem /dev/ttyUSB4G0); to_abandon/keenon4G.conf, check_net.conf; usr/bin/check_connect (usb0/ppp0 monitoring, start/stop keenon4G). max_4g_wait_response_time in interactive_params.yaml.
impact: Cellular fallback exists in older designs; may be unused on C40.
remediation: None.
description: The upstart keenon4G job itself is not installed by this package.

title: robotviz web UI (static Vue app) endpoints
evidence: /usr/share/robotviz: index.html title "Keenon", assets index/Home/Login/AboutModal .js; title string "Keenon Robot Mapping Tool"; roslib connections ws://192.168.64.20:9090 and :9091; calls /rosapi/*, /database/manager, /database/config_map, /robot_settings/cfg_launch_type_cmd, /robot_settings/cfg_origin_floor_cmd, /robot_settings/cfg_schedule_sw_cmd, /mx_config_srv, /reboot, /motor_lock, /manual_loop_closure, /operate_pbstream, /initialpose, /cmd_vel, /move_base/goal, /topo_action/*. Manifest type 3rdparty. HTTP server for the static files is not part of the package (nginx referenced by WsServer).
impact: A browser-based mapping/commissioning tool controls the robot directly through rosbridge, including drive (/cmd_vel), reboot, and config services.
remediation: Protect with network controls (see ROS-030, ROS-045).
description: STATIC_REFERENCE names.

title: Hard-coded sudo password inside send_depth_node binary
evidence: ELF string: shell command "echo <PASSWORD> | sudo -S service keenonrobot restart" (password: 11 lowercase chars, starts "ke", value redacted).
impact: Anyone with the package can learn a root/sudo password that is the same string used elsewhere (ROS-041, ROS-042); likely valid on production units (not verified).
remediation: Remove hard-coded passwords; use a restricted sudoers rule or service API; rotate the credential.
description: The same 11-character value also appears as the Wi-Fi AP passphrase and in WsServer; it is also the name of the main service, so it is trivially guessable.

title: Hard-coded password passed on command line to frpc_delete / sudo -S (WsServer and script)
evidence: WsServer ELF string: "/usr/bin/frpc_delete '<PASSWORD>' &" (11 chars, starts "ke", redacted); frpc_delete script: `keen=$1; echo ${keen}|sudo -S kill -9 $li`.
impact: Credential exposure in the binary and in process arguments (visible via ps).
remediation: Replace with root-owned service logic; no passwords in argv.
description: The password equals the value in ROS-040 (same 11-char string).

title: Default Wi-Fi AP credentials shipped in hostapd.conf (WPA-PSK), AP bridged to robot network
evidence: hostapd.conf: ssid=Keenon_robot_FFFFFF (suffix replaced by AP MAC), wpa=1, wpa_key_mgmt=WPA-PSK, wpa_pairwise=CCMP, wpa_passphrase=<11 chars, starts "ke", redacted>, bridge=br0; file is a dpkg conffile of robot-settings. Also wifi/wpa_supplicant.conf contains a 64-hex PSK for SSID "testAP" (starts "ca", redacted).
status: CONFIRMED (file); on-device value UNKNOWN (may be changed)
impact: If unchanged, anyone who knows the default passphrase (shared by all units, derived from a guessable string) joins the robot control LAN including unauthenticated rosbridge/ROS master.
remediation: Provision per-device random passphrases; use WPA2-only; do not bridge the AP to the control network.
description: wpa=1 selects WPA (v1) with CCMP.

title: Unauthenticated ROS master / rosbridge / services control (including config and reboot)
evidence: rosbridge authenticate=false (ROS-030). Services/topics reachable by name through rosbridge (STATIC_REFERENCE): robot_settings/launchConfig.srv (option, cmdKey, cmdValue -> edits launch config), /robot_settings/cfg_launch_type_cmd, /reboot, /motor_lock, /cmd_vel, /cfg_param_cmd, keenon_ui_msgs/param_update, cfg_param_info, database_operate (path,uuid), keenon_clean_msgs/OTA.srv (file_path, md5). ROS master is started by roslaunch with default port 11311 on ROS_IP 192.168.64.20 (upstart env).
status: CONFIRMED (interfaces exist); INFERRED (reachability and lack of access control)
impact: A LAN-adjacent attacker can drive the robot, change launch/robot-type configuration, trigger reboot or push OTA files.
remediation: Network segmentation, rosbridge auth, restrict service exposure.
description: No live validation was performed.

title: OTA update flow lacks integrity/authenticity controls and runs as root
evidence: manifest.json entries contain no hashes/signatures; debs contain only debian-binary, control.tar.gz, data.tar.xz (no signature members); ros_update uses md5 only ("check md5 success/failed", mbedtls_md5) with md5 supplied alongside the URL ("No obj url md5"); installs with `dpkg -i --force-confnew` then `apt-get -y -f install`, executes script/upgrade.sh, stops cron, reboots; manifest places bin/keenon at absolute dest /etc/init.d/ ; maintainer scripts run as root; robot-settings postinst executes `sudo cp` over files in /opt/ros/indigo/lib/python2.7/dist-packages.
impact: An attacker able to supply a package URL+md5 to ros_update (or tamper in transit/at rest) gets root code execution through maintainer scripts/init scripts.
remediation: Sign packages (detached signature verified on device), verify against pinned key, TLS + authentication for the update API.
description: Severity could be Critical if ros_update is proven reachable and unauthenticated; authentication was not analyzed.

title: robotviz login is client-side only with hard-coded key/ciphertext and pre-filled default credentials
evidence: Login.js: form state initialised with username "peanut" and a 6-digit numeric default password (starts "12", redacted); onLogin compares AES-ECB encryption of the JSON form object (CryptoJS, key const = 8-char string starting "PE", parsed as hex) to a hard-coded 96-hex-char constant (starts "52"); on match router pushes /home. No server round-trip.
status: CONFIRMED (code); whether the constant corresponds to the default credentials NOT_ANALYZED
impact: Authentication can be bypassed by anyone with browser dev tools or by connecting to rosbridge directly; the secret material is in the client bundle.
remediation: Do real server-side authentication; remove defaults.
description: The effective key of CryptoJS Hex.parse(<8-char key string>) is only 4 bytes (non-hex characters parse to 0) - INFERRED from library semantics, LOW confidence.

title: CoAP bridge builds sudo shell commands and downloads archives by URL without signature
evidence: Strings: `echo "` / `" | sudo -S sh -c "` / `chmod -R `, /etc/ros/runtime/database/uuidzip/, /tmp/robot/, /work/robot/, QLTftp curl_easy_perform; topic /libcoap/download (url, md5) with md5 only.
impact: Download URLs/paths flow into root shell commands; md5 gives integrity only against corruption.
remediation: Use execve with argument arrays, sign downloads, restrict who can publish /libcoap/download.
description: Password operand source of the `sudo -S` pipe was not recovered.

title: Samba shares exposing /home/peanut and /root/.ros (read-write) and /etc/ros/runtime
evidence: smb.conf: [old log path] path=/root/.ros read only=no; [config] path=/etc/ros/runtime read only=yes; [home] path=/home/peanut read only=no; guest ok=no; map to guest = bad user; unix password sync = yes. postinst: `if [ -d "$myPath"]; then cp $SMBCONF_FILE /etc/samba/` - $myPath is undefined and there is no space before `]`; bash evaluates `[ -d "" ]` as the one-argument form `[ -d ]` which is true, so the copy runs if /etc/samba exists (INFERRED, not executed).
status: CONFIRMED (config); INFERRED (copy executes); Samba presence/users UNKNOWN
impact: If Samba is installed and a weak password exists, remote read/write of home, root-owned log dir and runtime configs is possible.
remediation: Remove shares or restrict to localhost; use strong unique credentials.
description: Shares require Samba authentication (guest ok = no).

title: Device nodes created world read/write (MODE 0666) by udev rules and scripts
evidence: 56-orbbec.rules MODE:="0666" for Orbbec USB; 50-usb-debug.rules ttyUSB 067b:2303 MODE 0666 -> ttyUSBDebug (getty login console via keenonUsbDebug.conf template); auto_make_port.py rule template MODE:="0666", GROUP:="dialout"; ydlidar-ros-driver usr/startup/initenv.sh writes ydlidar*.rules MODE 0666.
impact: Any local user can access serial/USB devices including the STM32 and debug console.
remediation: Use group-restricted modes.
description: No world-writable regular files exist in the debs (checked all 7,879 file entries: only modes 644/755, plus 44 symlinks at 777; no setuid/setgid).

title: End-of-life software stack
evidence: ros-indigo (EOL Apr 2019), Ubuntu 14.04 trusty (EOL 2019), Python 2.7 scripts (print statements; libpython2.7), libssl.so.1.0.0/libcrypto.so.1.0.0 (OpenSSL 1.0.x) in ros_update/libcoap, Boost 1.54, OpenCV 2.4, PCL 1.7 and 1.8.1.99, Go 1.16.2 frpc, libcpprest 2.10, websocketpp 0.8.2, nlohmann json 3.11 in 3 binaries.
impact: Known unpatched vulnerabilities likely exist in system libraries; cannot be remediated within this package.
remediation: Plan platform upgrade; isolate network exposure meanwhile.
description: CVE mapping was not performed (no network access).

title: Debian packages unsigned; control files carry no md5sums; manifest has no checksums
evidence: Every deb ar members = debian-binary, control.tar.gz, data.tar.xz; no _gpg* members; no other control files besides control/maintainer scripts/conffiles (checked all 106).
impact: No offline way to verify provenance of the 106 debs.
remediation: Add signing and checksums.
description: Integrity relies on the single md5 supplied at update time.

title: Wvdial guest/guest credentials and legacy SSH public key shipped
evidence: wvdial.conf Username/Password both "guest" (carrier APN placeholder); system/robot.pub: ssh-rsa public key, 401 bytes, not referenced by any script in the package (grep of authorized_keys/robot.pub found only roslaunch remoteprocess.py).
impact: Guest credentials are low value; the public key may be an authorized key used by the vendor (usage UNKNOWN).
remediation: Remove unused keys/files.
description: Public keys are not secrets; no private key was found (searched for BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY).

title: Postinst overwrites system libraries and binaries with vendor copies
evidence: sudo rm/cp of rosbridge_library/protocol.py, internal/publishers.py, tornado/iostream.py into /opt/ros/indigo/lib/python2.7/dist-packages; replaces /opt/ros/indigo/lib/tf2_web_republisher/tf2_web_republisher (x64/arm32 variants, chmod 755); copies librosconsole.so into /opt/ros/indigo/lib; removes /usr/local/lib/libusb*; edits /etc/bash.bashrc (HISTTIMEFORMAT), /etc/os-release, /etc/udev/rules.d/50-keenon.rules (truncated), runs `python config_setting.py`, `python yaml_setting.py`, user_monitor_update.sh.
impact: Non-package-managed file replacement breaks package integrity tracking and makes rollbacks hard.
remediation: Package the patches properly.
description: Contents of the patched files were not diffed against upstream.

title: Thermal trip points raised and ADB re-enabled by user_monitor script
evidence: user_monitor.sh: writes 90000 to thermal_zone0/trip_point_0_temp and 100000 to trip_point_1_temp every 5 s; restarts /etc/init.d/adbd.sh if the USB gadget UDC is empty. user_monitor_update.sh copies it to /etc/init.d when /etc/fw_version < v1.0.9.
status: CONFIRMED (script); whether installed on units UNKNOWN
impact: Overrides SoC thermal protections (safety/durability) and keeps an ADB interface alive.
remediation: Review thermal limits with SoC vendor; disable ADB in production.
description: Script is in the to_abandon list but still installed to /usr/bin.

title: All robot services run as root; unlimited core dumps written to /home/peanut/keenon/core
evidence: Upstart jobs run as root; `ulimit -c unlimited`; core_pattern set to /home/peanut/keenon/core/core-%e-%p-%t; post-stop `kill -9` of all processes matching "opt/ros".
impact: Any ROS node compromise yields root; core dumps may leak memory contents (maps, credentials).
remediation: Drop privileges for nodes; restrict core dump location/permissions.

title: Build-environment path leakage and bundled debug symbols
evidence: Strings like /workdir/catkin_ws/src/keenon_ros/keenon_infrastructure/rest_kits/..., keenon_interface/ros2cmd/libcoap/...; busy-map deb contains ./workdir/catkin_ws/** (28 entries); fdl-ros ships /usr/lib/debug/... symbol copies; unstripped: libOpenNI2, liborbbec, libudev, libusb copies, libsy_tof_dev_sdk.so (11,031 symbols), micro-laser firmware ELFs (1,176/1,898 symbols).
impact: Eases reverse engineering of those components; reveals internal source tree names.
remediation: Strip binaries before release.
description: Other binaries (90 ARM executables) are stripped.

title: Packaging anomaly: ros-indigo-remote-tools deb declares Package: build
evidence: control: Package: build, Source: build (0.0.0-0trusty), Description: "The remote ssh package", Version 2.3.1c1-4573-g1406f3b-trusty; installed-size 8827 kB. File list: WsServer, frpc_release_arm, update_frpc.py, update_map_frpc.py, frpc_delete, frpc_info.ini, 2 upstart confs.
impact: dpkg registers it as "build" (generic name, collision/overwrite risk; hard to identify during forensics).
remediation: Rename the package.

title: Remote-tools tunnel client and command stack executes strings built from message fields
evidence: update_map_frpc.py: set_file_value(msg) does `eval(data_json)["data"]["config"]` on a JSON string passed on argv (Python 2 eval), and writes arbitrary key/value pairs into /etc/ros/runtime/frpc_info.ini (frp config) which can define arbitrary tunnels (type, local_ip, local_port, remote_port, plugin). update_frpc.py writes server_addr/server_port/remote_port/token from argv into the frp ini.
impact: Given control of the websocket message (ROS-032), arbitrary Python expression evaluation and arbitrary local-port exposure through frp become possible.
remediation: Use json.loads and a whitelist of ini fields.
description: Reachability of the message source depends on ROS-032 exposure.

title: Fixed cloud broker IP and test topic names shipped in production configuration
evidence: mqtt_server_ip: 47.96.156.255; sub_server_topic elevtopic_test; pub_server_topic robottopic_test (all 30 model directories).
impact: Production units may talk to a test topic namespace; endpoint is hard-wired.
remediation: Make configurable.
description: See ROS-035.

title: Native binary inventory (ELF)
evidence: Scanned data.tar of all 106 debs: 283 ELF (186 shared objects/DYN, 97 EXEC). 266 stripped ARM32; unstripped: 10 ARM32 libs, 2 ARM32 firmware ELFs, 3 RISC-V32 firmware ELFs; 2 x86-64 (robot-settings x64 tf2_web_republisher and X86 check_mx_stereo). 90 stripped ARM executables: ROS node executables, helper tools (usb_scan, module_tool, fixture_calibrate, as_nuwacam_node, fdl_calibration_node, nmon, ethtool, schedule-reset, mx_config, check_mx_stereo), ros_update, WsServer and frpc_release_arm (Go, no DT_NEEDED). Per-binary list in ros_packages.md section 5.4.
impact: All binaries are closed-source vendor builds; analysis limited to headers/symbols/strings.
remediation: Use Ghidra on selected binaries (ros_update, WsServer, coap_bridge_server, chassis) for deeper work.
description: No disassembly or decompilation was performed.

title: Bundled third-party code and versions
evidence: peanut-localization ships libpcl_*.so.1.8.1.99 (29 MB libpcl_features etc.) while other nodes link libpcl_*.so.1.7; ros_update/WsServer embed websocketpp 0.8.2 + asio + mbedtls md5; libcpprest.so.2.10; coap_bridge via libcoap (+libcurl); frpc Go 1.16.2 with fatedier/frp; nlohmann json 3.11.2 in depth_laser_cali_node, astra_camera_node, calibration_node; libkzipc embeds miniz; show_points/module_tool embed libsodium (crypto_secretbox); cartographer links protobuf .so.14, cairo, lua5.2, glog/gflags; costmap/TEB/navfn are upstream ROS indigo code (versions 1.12.14 etc.).
impact: Mixed PCL ABI versions on one device; any CVE audit must cover these bundles.
remediation: SBOM generation recommended.

title: micro_laser firmware blobs are Linux userland ELF apps for the line-laser modules (RISC-V32 and ARM32)
evidence: ql_xd1q_v821_33_33_20260603, ql_xd1q_v821_33_35_20260603, ql_xd1q_v821_3_34_20260603: ELF32 RISC-V (e_machine 243), musl (/lib/ld-musl-riscv32.so.1), 306,112 bytes, symtab 1,176 symbols, build string "Jun  5 2026 12:08:19", classes App_V3s_7251_Vga_X1_XD1Q, hHandleCMD, tcp_server_*, uart_parse_frame; strings: upload/replace /root/main and /root/config.txt, "dmesg | grep Linux version", gpio 135 export. ql_xd1q_202_35 and ql_xd1q_2_33: ARM32 ELF (260,936 bytes). auto_bind_node/micro_laser_node strings: "(5/5) Update firmware ...", SN read, left/right auto-binding, GPIO power restart, /dev/ttyACM0..3.
impact: The robot pushes executable firmware to external Linux-based sensor modules over the CDC-ACM serial link at start-up; integrity of that push is unauthenticated by design (INFERRED).
remediation: Treat module firmware as part of the supply chain; sign.
description: The build date string (Jun 5 2026) shows this release was built mid-2026.

title: Vendor depth-camera SDK blobs bundled in fdl-ros (Orbbec OpenNI2, Berxel)
evidence: fdl-ros lib/fdl/arm32: libfdl.so (contains JSON config text with "host_url":"192.168.64.199:9090"), libdepthsInterface.so, libmapobs.so, libfruit.so, libRobotOperation.a, sensors/depthAB/OpenNI2/Drivers/{liborbbec.so,libOniFile.so,orbbec.ini,libusb-1.0*,libudev*}, sensors/depthBS/{libBerxelUvcDriver.so,params100Q.bin 6,144,000 bytes}; /usr/lib/debug copies with symbols; berxel-camera ships libBerxelHawk and params100Q.bin.
impact: Drop/cliff detection relies on a depth camera SDK with its own USB stack copies (libusb/libudev) shadowing system ones; postinst deletes /usr/local/lib/libusb*.
remediation: Ensure library path ordering does not load the wrong libusb.

title: Embedded protocol/crypto use: ZeroMQ+libsodium to MX module; md5 only in OTA
evidence: send_depth_node and module_tool: strings tcp://%s:%s, crypto_secretbox / crypto_secretbox_open, username/password length checks (username.length () <= UCHAR_MAX) consistent with a ZeroMQ/libsodium based RPC; ros_update/libcoap use mbedtls_md5 / libkmd5 for integrity.
impact: MX stereo module link is encrypted with a symmetric secretbox (key source unknown) and also reachable by anonymous FTP for parameter files.
remediation: Review key management.
